decisions.rationale: OM4 multimode fiber is recommended because 400 m exceeds the 100 m copper limit but is within the assignment's 101–400 m backbone band. 10GBASE-SR commonly uses 850 nm optics; verify OM4 reach, connector loss and optical budget.
decisions.transceiver_rationale: 10GBASE-T is the copper PHY; 10GBASE-SR uses short-reach multimode optics (850 nm); 10GBASE-LR/ER are single-mode reach classes whose exact choice depends on distance and the calculated optical loss budget.

topology_caveats: A collapsed core may be suitable depending on actual scale.

routing_caveats: If the network grows to multiple sites or external routing domains, reassess the routing design.
redundancy_actions: Provide redundant uplinks between access, distribution and core.
Use an appropriate loop-prevention mechanism such as Rapid PVST+.
Test link failure and avoid unintended Layer 2 loops.

Conventional LAN subnetting reserves network and broadcast addresses.
Media distance bands follow the assignment; final optics require compatibility and optical-budget verification.
